name: Baltic Trail – Szlak Rowerowy Wokół Bałtyku (R10 / EuroVelo 10 / Velo Baltica, Poland)
distance_note: about 588 km including the Hel Peninsula (about 533 km on the shorter variant without it); sources vary
summary: The Polish stretch of EuroVelo 10 follows the Baltic coast from Świnoujście on the German border to the Vistula Lagoon and Braniewo. Expect a mix of coastal cycle paths, forest tracks and some sandy sections.
facts: R10 is the common Polish name for the Polish section of EuroVelo 10, the loop around the Baltic Sea; Velo Baltica mainly refers to the part in West Pomerania.
The whole EuroVelo 10 loop is about 9,100 km through nine countries, and it has no fixed start point or direction.
The Polish section is given as about 588 km including the Hel Peninsula, or about 533 km on the shorter variant without it.

In Poland the route runs through West Pomeranian, Pomeranian and Warmian-Masurian voivodeships, passing Świnoujście, Międzyzdroje, Dziwnów, Rewal, Kołobrzeg, Darłowo, Ustka, Łeba, Władysławowo, Gdynia, Sopot, Gdańsk, Elbląg, Frombork and Braniewo.
Despite its name, R10 often leaves the immediate seashore, which some riders criticise.
notes: Surface is mixed: asphalt, gravel, forest tracks, and some sandy or muddy patches. The Rowy–Łeba stretch is often described as one of the weakest, with earth, sand and worn slabs, so a tyre that can handle gravel helps.
Terrain is mostly flat, so daily distances of about 60–100 km are realistic. Many riders cover the Polish coast in roughly 6–8 days.
The route swings inland in several places, so carry food and water for stretches away from beach towns. Resort towns are the easiest places to resupply.
days_hint: Roughly 6–8 days for the Polish section at 60–100 km per day (traveller reports and stage plans)
